analysis:
All four changed files are test-only (ProviderCoreTests). They add assertions or tests for prefill geometry: the report schema v5 fields prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep with schema-4 decode compatibility, the benchmark fixture environment pinning the 512 chunk and 2048 step budget when a stripe is pinned, the live-runner engine environment pinning the simulated geometry, and the paged-pool maxPrefillChunk lockstep with the Gemma 4 wide plain chunk (EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift around lines 713-754). None of these touch production code, the coordinator-provider wire, key handling, attestation, App Attest authorization, or the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041). No changes to encryption, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, scoping or purge paths. The tests use synthetic models and a /tmp synthetic root, with no secrets or network I/O.

No new attack surface or security regression is identified in the supplied evidence. Remaining unverified contract: the production source changes that these tests exercise (EngineV2Factory prefillGeometry, widePrefillChunkTokens, the pool sizing in prepareProductionBackend, and SchedulerPrefillDecisionLiveRunner.engineEnvironment) are outside this batch. A pass over those files should confirm that the paged KV ring and pool sizing, which follows max(chunk, stripe), is not reduced, since an undersized pool could abort the daemon (availability). The tests assert it is preserved. No security conclusion depends on this batch alone.
